root.name: Van Geet Opening: Novosibirsk Variation
root.moves: 1. Nc3 c5 2. d4 cxd4 3. Qxd4 Nc6 4. Qh4

overview: White swaps the d-pawn for the c-pawn, then brings the queen to h4 to gain a tempo on nothing in particular and eye the kingside. Black gets easy development and a lead from ...Nf6 and ...e5. It is an offbeat line played for surprise rather than an edge.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Bf4 or Bg5 and avoid queen harassment
Use the queen on h4 to pin pieces on the kingside

black_ideas.idea: Develop with tempo against the queen with ...Nf6 or ...e5

typical_structures.structure: Open game after c- and d-pawns are traded

character.notes: An odd development with no forcing play.

soundness.notes: Likely equal but a tempo behind.

structure.notes: c- and d-pawns exchanged leaves open lines.

level.notes: Not a beginner choice because the queen is exposed.
